result.title: Contextual Non-Convex Bandit Optimization with Two-Point Feedback
result.summary: We study a non-stochastic contextual bandit problem with Lipschitz losses. At every round, the learner observes the context then picks two actions, observes the difference between their losses, and incurs their mean. The aim is to minimize the regret against a generic non-parametric comparator class of policies mapping contexts to actions; for example, Lipschitz policies and Hölder-smooth policies. We show how relying on a hierarchical discretization technique allows us to improve upon the regret rates achievable under one-point feedback, and even recover the full-information rate in some cases; notably, for sufficiently smooth policy classes or low-dimensional instances. Additionally, for Lipschitz policies, we present an algorithm whose per-round computational complexity is only logarithmic in the time horizon.

AI.brief_summary: 研究 Lipschitz 损失下的非随机上下文 bandit：每轮依上下文选两个动作、只观测二者损失之差并承担均值损失，借助分层离散化为 Lipschitz、Hölder 等非参数策略类改进 regret，部分情形下可达到全信息速率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「两点差分反馈」与分层离散化可能为 latent 推理轨迹在仅成对比较监督下的信用分配与样本效率分析提供概念工具，但原文与视觉推理无直接联系，可迁移性需核查。
